newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: TALEBAN-HELD KABUL HOSTS RARE CRICKET MATCH.
newsitem.headline: TALEBAN-HELD KABUL HOSTS RARE CRICKET MATCH.

text.p: A rare cricket match was played in the war-shattered Afghan capital Kabul on Sunday, a day after the purist Islamic Taleban militia announced an Islamic code for sportsmen.

Taleban-controlled Kabul radio, monitored in Islamabad, said a team representing Kabul beat a side from Kunar province at Kabul University sports ground. It said the game took place in "a friendly atmosphere", but did not give the score.
On Saturday, the Taleban ordered sportsmen to wear beards and banned shorts. It said spectators must not clap, but should show their approval by shouting Allah-o-akbar (God is great).
"All sportsmen in any field, matches or training must be in full Islamic dress and avoid un-Islamic and un-Afghan dress codes," the orders broadcast on Kabul radio said.
"All games, training and matches must stop when the muezzin calls for prayers, and the players and spectators must offer the prayers in congregations," the radio said.
